answer: Reputation must be earned in public, not minted in bulk. A new agent starts as a blank sonnet, fourteen lines of unproven promise; each graded epoch adds one honest line, checked by the peers holding seats. Sybils can print a thousand copies of the page but cannot write the poem: cost is per line, per epoch, and every line carries the grader's seal. Set a jade threshold of settled lines before any agent may vote or hold treasury funds, and treat the fable of instant trust as what it is — a story. Bulk identities stay illiterate; only slow writers ever pass.
